newsitem.title: USA: Kaiser cites lack of hedging for Q3 loss.
newsitem.headline: Kaiser cites lack of hedging for Q3 loss.

text.p: Kaiser Aluminum Corp Wednesday reported a loss of $0.12 per share for the third quarter, citing its lack of hedging activities late last year.
Chief executive George T. Haymaker Jr. said the unsatisfactory results were in line with the expectations Kaiser announced on October 7 when the company projected a loss of $0.14 to $0.20 per share.
At that time, Kaiser said its fourth quarter loss could substantially exceed the third quarter loss if prices of primary aluminum do not increase from recent levels.
The latest loss compares to a profit of $0.13 per share in 1995's September quarter. Sales for the third quarter totaled $553.4 million, compared with $550.3 million a year earlier.

The company said its loss in the third quarter was largely a reflection of weak market prices for primary aluminum, noting the average cash price for primary aluminum on the London Metal Exchange during the quarter was 21 percent below that of the year-ago period and 6 percent below that of the second quarter of this year.

In addition, Kaiser said, its average realized price for alumina, which is significantly influenced by primary aluminum prices, was more than 9 percent below the level of both the year-ago period and the second quarter of this year.

"The weakness in market prices had an unfavorable impact on the company's results because, in anticipation of improving market conditions, Kaiser entered 1996 with a larger-than-customary amount of its alumina and primary metal unprotected by forward sales or hedges," Haymaker said.
"Such market conditions did not materialize, and the company was exposed in the third quarter to further declines in metal prices," he said.

Kaiser said its third quarter was also hurt by a number of other factors, including: lower-than-planned shipments of aluminum can stock due mainly to softness in demand; high operating costs associated with disruptions in power supply at the 65 percent owned Alpart alumina refinery in Jamaica; and high natural gas prices at the Gramercy, La., alumina refinery.
MAXXAM Inc holds about 62 percent of Kaiser on a fully diluted basis. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
